content:
I fully admit my DIY iPhone camera mod looks pretty silly—but it genuinely makes using my iPhone for photography more practical and more fun.

It started as a solution to one specific video-shooting problem, but I ended up using it way more times than I expected…

One of the biggest divides in the compact camera world has always been whether or not to have a viewfinder. Back in the day, camera enthusiasts would get quite heated debating whether an electronic viewfinder (EVF) or an optical viewfinder was better, but EVFs have improved so much that nobody really bothers with that argument anymore.

But whether optical or electronic, a viewfinder offers one very practical advantage over composing shots with the rear screen—especially when you're shooting under harsh sunlight. Even with the screen brightness cranked all the way up, it's still hard to see what you're capturing in strong sunlight, and you may also have to deal with screen glare.

Although here in London, this hasn't really been a big issue for me before. But this summer brought record-breaking heatwaves, and honestly, the last time I saw a cloud or any rain feels like it was about thirty years ago.

But for me, the issue goes beyond that. There's a psychological difference between looking through a viewfinder where you only see what's in the frame, versus using the rear screen where you're also aware of the surroundings around you. Sometimes it's exactly this difference that makes me reach for a dedicated camera rather than my iPhone.

When I was choosing a camcorder a few years ago, the Blackmagic Pocket Cinema Camera 4K was clearly the standout winner, but the lack of a viewfinder gave me pause. In the end I decided it wasn't a big deal for me, because I mostly use it indoors, and rigging up an external monitor with a sun hood covers most outdoor scenarios.

But there are still times when I want to use it without hauling the whole rig with the monitor attached. So I found a simple accessory specifically designed for outdoor use. It's a two-in-one sun hood and magnifying loupe that magnetically attaches to the camera's rear screen, instantly turning it into an optical viewfinder.

I had an upcoming shoot where I needed to record video with both the BMPCC 4K and my iPhone 16 Pro Max at the same time. After a quick test at the venue, the viewfinder accessory really came in handy. Since the BMPCC 4K and the iPhone have very similar screen sizes, I wondered if this accessory would work just as well on the iPhone.

Of course, the iPhone doesn't have a magnetic attachment system, but the iPhone is light enough that holding the loupe manually against it is no problem at all. To my surprise, it worked surprisingly well—especially since I use the Camera Control button as my shutter.

I soon found myself reaching for it in quite a few situations. I love the convenience of being able to actually see the screen clearly even in harsh sunlight, and that immersive feeling. My iPhone became my main camera a long time ago, and with this DIY mod, I feel like even more occasions are covered just by using my phone.

Crazy or genius? I'd love to hear your thoughts in the comments. If you're in the latter camp, unfortunately the product I bought seems to have been discontinued, and I haven't seen anything similar designed for screens larger than three inches. If you find one, please drop a link in the comments.
